symbols.name: ShadowShellManager

claims.text: Represents a completed task on a dedicated git branch.
claims.why: The class is named CandidateBranch and has branch_name, worktree_path, task, completed, error, score fields; it is used in run_task to represent the result.

claims.text: Spawns an adapter and runs the agent inside a given GitWorktree.
claims.why: The class docstring states that. The run_task method creates a worktree, creates a session with cwd set to worktree path, and processes events.

claims.text: Executes the agent task inside a new worktree and returns a CandidateBranch.
claims.why: The method creates a worktree, runs the agent, and returns a CandidateBranch instance.

claims.text: The task is the initial one-shot prompt. Crucially, ``cwd`` is the worktree, and the adapter is required to honor it at process launch.
claims.why: The claim about adapter honoring cwd is not verifiable from this chunk; it depends on the adapter implementation.

claims.text: Commit any changes the agent made in the worktree
claims.why: The comment says 'Commit any changes', but the code calls self.worktree_manager.commit_candidate; the behavior of commit_candidate is not defined in this chunk.
The commit message is exactly that string, with task interpolated.

observations.what: CandidateBranch has a default 'completed' field set to False, but in run_task it is set to True only on success. The error branch sets completed=False explicitly, which is consistent.
The run_task method sets session_config['cwd'] to str(worktree_path); this assumes worktree_path is a Path, which is true from its type hint and the return of create_worktree.

The method always calls self.adapter.terminate(session_id) in the finally block, but if terminate raises, the cleanup_worktree in the inner finally may be skipped if candidate.completed is False (because the inner finally is part of the outer try). Actually, the inner finally will execute even if terminate raises because it's a finally block; but if terminate raises an exception, that exception propagates after the inner finally, and the outer finally's code after the inner finally might not run? Actually, the structure is: outer try-except-finally: inside the try, there's a try-except-finally. The outer finally executes after the inner finally regardless. The cleanup_worktree is inside the outer finally, so it will run even if terminate raises. However, if terminate raises, the exception propagates after the outer finally, so the function exits with an exception. That may be acceptable.

The run_task method assumes that adapter.events will eventually yield a SessionEnded event; if it doesn't, it raises RuntimeError. But if the async for loop exits without encountering SessionEnded, exit_event remains None and the error is raised. However, if the events stream raises an exception before yielding SessionEnded, that exception propagates out of the loop and is caught by the except Exception block, setting candidate.error. That is handled.
The claim 'the adapter is required to honor it at process launch' refers to the cwd setting; this is not checkable from this file.
